content:
aisha: Heads-up — enabling torch.compile + CUDA graphs on the 70B job caused 20-35% tail latency regressions for variable-length chat sessions.
kevin: repro script?
maya: repro + perf traces would help. I assume this is shape churn between requests?
aisha: attaching short repro steps inline. Observed behavior: warmup with seq=128 then first real request jumps to seq=1024 -> kernel selection flips to long-seq kernels and CUDA graph replay yields worse occupancy.
benchbot: quick bench run attached: https://bench.internal/runs/175210-ctg
aisha: repro steps:
```
# run warmup with short seq
python run_infer.py --model redwood-70b --seq 128 --iters 50
# then send variable-length sessions
python run_infer.py --model redwood-70b --seq 1024 --iters 10 --use_torch_compile --use_cudagraph
```
kevin: can you paste the profiler snippet (nvprof / nsight) showing kernel time breakdown?
maya: also include KV cache behavior — switching to long seq often changes kv stride and changes matmul kernel selection.
aisha: profiler excerpt (trimmed):
```
% time  kernel   grid   block   time(ms)
45%    matmul_fwd_k128  ...  12.3
30%    matmul_fwd_k512  ...  18.9
15%    kv_update        ...  6.1
10%    other            ...  4.0
```
Note: after torch.compile the graph captured the k128 matmul path, but when seq grows the runtime attempted to remap to k512 and CUDA graph replay doesn't rebind tensors, causing extra copies and kernel mismatch.
tim: sounds like two interacting things: 1) graph capture/slotting binding assumptions 2) kernel-autotuner choosing different kernels mid-session. We should ensure graph capture uses representative max-shapes or re-capture on shape bucket changes.
kevin: idea: maintain small shape-bucketed caches for CUDA graphs keyed by (seq_len_bucket, batch, dtype). When change detected, fallback to tracing code path that does dynamic dispatch (no graph) and trigger async re-capture.
maya: agree. Also our kernel selector needs to be compile-aware: if a compiled graph was captured, prefer kernels compatible with captured strides even if autotune says otherwise, or schedule a recompile of the graph with the autotuned kernel for the new shape.
benchbot: ran autoselect experiment: forcing k512 for both warmup and long requests brought tail back to baseline. numbers: p95 down 28%.
aisha: this suggests the autotuner picks different kernel for short vs long seq. But dynamic graphs + static capture confuses the runtime mapping.
kevin: short-term mitigation: detect mismatch during graph replay and fall back to non-graph path with a warning. Long-term: add "capture-hint" to kernel selection that picks kernels stable across adjacent sequence lengths unless a hard perf win is measured in steady-state.
tim: also consider KV cache layout: if kv cache is sharded differently for long sequences, that changes alignment and causes new kernel path. We should include kv_layout in the graph key.
maya: perf regression ticket: PERF-4892. Assigning owners: aisha (investigation), kevin (kernel selector changes), maya (graph/capture and KV cache layout).
kevin: plan of attack:
1) reproduce minimal script + bench harness (aisha)
2) run autotune trace across seq buckets [64,128,256,512,1024] and record kernel picks (kevin)
3) add graph-keying prototype to include seq_bucket + kv_layout (maya)
4) run end-to-end with torch.compile + graphs + kv changes (tim)

benchbot: quick note: quantized path (int8) didn't regress, so this seems FP16 kernel selection specific.
aisha: filing a short PR to gate CUDA graph replay when shape_bucket changes; tests in CI will catch replays with mismatched kernel types.
maya: one more idea — train the kernel autotuner to prefer kernels that are robust to small stride/shape changes (lower variance) when graphs are enabled.
kevin: agreed. I'll instrument the autotuner to expose a "stability score" and add a knob to prefer stability over raw throughput for graph-captured models.
tim: ok team — let's aim for a mitigative patch this week and a longer-term autotuner change next cycle.
aisha: thanks all, I'll paste logs + nvprof links into PERF-4892.
